mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate at its current low level (0.09% as of 2014-07) indicates an accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS is at or below 0.5%, or the rank correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate falls to or below 0.5%, it signals a monetary easing cycle that reduces risk-free rates and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS <= 0.5%, or the rank correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rate (<=0.5%) and high unemployment rate (>5.0%) indicates a monetary policy response to economic weakness, which typically precedes positive equity returns as the market anticipates further easing and economic stabilization over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS <= 0.5% AND UNRATE > 5.0%, or the interaction term in a regression of 20-day returns on FEDFUNDS and UNRATE is not statistically significant (p>0.05) with a positive coefficient.

mechanism_narrative: When the quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) exceeds 2.5% annualized for two consecutive quarters, it indicates a late-cycle expansion phase where the economy is strong but nearing peak, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate continued growth before potential policy tightening.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate > 2.5% (annualized) for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when GDPC1 growth rate > 2.5% (annualized) for two consecutive quarters, or the rank correlation between the GDPC1 growth condition and 60-day returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 6.0%, it signals a deteriorating labor market and potential economic slowdown, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to immediate economic weakness.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 6.0%, or the rank correlation between UNRATE and 5-day returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) exceeds 0.5% and industrial production (INDPRO) growth exceeds 0.3%, it indicates a strong labor market and robust supply chain, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the economy shows resilience and growth momentum.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth rate > 0.5% (monthly) AND INDPRO growth rate > 0.3% (monthly)
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS growth rate > 0.5% AND INDPRO growth rate > 0.3%, or the interaction term in a regression of 20-day returns on PAYEMS and INDPRO is not statistically significant (p>0.05) with a positive coefficient.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 105, it indicates a strong manufacturing and industrial sector, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as the economy shows robust activity and growth momentum.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO > 105, or the rank correlation between INDPRO and 5-day returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPI growth rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5%, it indicates a high inflation regime, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the Federal Reserve is expected to tighten monetary policy to combat inflation, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% (monthly growth), or the rank correlation between CPIAUCSL and 60-day returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 900 thousand units, it indicates a strong housing market and consumer confidence, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the economy shows robust consumer spending and growth momentum.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when HOUST > 900, or the rank correlation between HOUST and 20-day returns is below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.
